The 6 Pillars Glossary

          
Click any card to inspect the breakdown.

The Wires

            
#01

          

          
Model Context Protocol (MCP)

          

            

What:
 An open standard to connect AI models to external tools and internal data.

            

Analogy:
 The universal USB-C port for artificial intelligence.

            

Why it matters:
 Connect your tools once and use them with any modern AI agent.

            
Takeaway: Standard protocols beat vendor lock-in every time.

          

        

        

        

          

            
The Engine

            
#02

          

          
Tokens

          

            

What:
 The atomic pieces of words that language models read and write.

            

Analogy:
 Lego bricks or syllables of machine language.

            

Why it matters:
 Token count directly dictates your cloud bills and model speed.

            
Takeaway: Tokens are compute currency. Keep context trimmed.

          

        

        

        

          

            
The Engine

            
#03

          

          
Context Window

          

            

What:
 The maximum number of tokens an AI can see at one time.

            

Analogy:
 The size of the physical desk where the AI is working.

            

Why it matters:
 When overloaded, earlier instructions drop off or degrade.

            
Takeaway: A bigger desk helps, but a clean desk prevents errors.

          

        

        

        

          

            
The Brain

            
#04

          

          
Skills & Rules Hierarchy

          

            

What:
 Modular instruction folders loaded only when specifically needed.

            

Analogy:
 Standard Operating Procedure manuals stored on a bookshelf.

            

Why it matters:
 Keeps the main context tiny while enabling deep expertise on demand.

            
Takeaway: Load knowledge surgically, not all at once.

          

        

        

        

          

            
The Society

            
#05

          

          
Orchestrator-Worker Loops

          

            

What:
 Dividing a complex task between specialized sub-agents.

            

Analogy:
 A general contractor managing an electrician and a plumber.

            

Why it matters:
 Prevents one giant context from getting tangled and confused.

            
Takeaway: Specialized small agents beat one monolithic prompt.

          

        

        

        

          

            
The Armor

            
#06

          

          
Falsifiable Verifiers

          

            

What:
 Independent deterministic checks that must be able to fail.

            

Analogy:
 A smoke detector that you deliberately test with test smoke.

            

Why it matters:
 A verification step that cannot fail is just decorative theater.

            
Takeaway: The verifier must never be the producer.
